object.name: evi.overdrive.tanh~
object.digest: High quality anti-aliased tanh-based saturation with drive, input/output gain wrapping and filter shaping
object.description: The most luxurious of the evieve 'overdrive' objects, with drive, gain wrapping, additional input/output gain shaping and two damping filters which behave like a crossover, making it possible to control the amount of saturated and dry signal in the final output. The saturator is a tanh-like approximation with antiderivative anti-aliasing and oversampling options. <o>evi.overdrive.tanh~</o> can be driven very hard and tonally shaped very easily making it a versatile nonlinear processor for a wide range of use cases. It is of course quite expensive.
object.discussion: For more information about evieve Overdrive processors and other saturation types see the 'evieve overdrive' tab of the helpfile.

inlets.description: Linear gain 1..100. This actually controls a gain staging around the internal saturator. The object handles high gain very well with minimal aliasing. This inlet corresponds to the equivalent inlet of the 'evi.overdrive.atan~' object.

outlets.digest: Tanh(x)-based Saturation Out - anti-aliased for your audio not for Maths

messages.name: history
messages.digest: Top level gen~ [history] / History() declarations can be reset by messages to the object

attributes.name: aa
attributes.description: The 'aa' ('Anti-Aliasing) method used. 0=Adaa1, 1=Adaa1 2x oversampled, 2=Adaa1 4x oversampled, 3=Adaa2 (default), 4=Adaa2 2x oversampled, 5=Adaa2 4x oversampled. 0..5 does not necessarily mean increasing in quality, it really depends on your audio input material. Experimentation is encouraged.

attributes.name: hfcompensate
attributes.description: The object provides a high frequency compensation 'decorelation' filter on its output for restoring the reduced high frequency response that can occur with this type of anti-aliasing, especially when utilising the oversampling options (as opposed to just using pure 'adaa'). Experiment with turning this on to improve high frequencies (default on).

attributes.name: highcutoff
attributes.description: Two filters act like a crossover, summing some dry signal back into the saturated path and controlling how much input signal reaches the saturator. @highcutoff controls the high cut filter (lowpass), lower Hz values will greatly darken the sound.

attributes.name: highdamp
attributes.description: Two filters act like a crossover, summing some dry signal back into the saturated path and controlling how much input signal reaches the saturator. @highdamp controls the shelving chracteristic of the high cut (lowpass) filter. If @highdamp == 0, the filter is bypassed, if @highdamp == 1 the filter is a full lowpass and the cutting effect very strong. 0..1 @highdamp is an increasingly damping shelf filter.

attributes.name: io
attributes.description: An additional gain stage that is reciprocal around input / output. If @io is > 0, input gain (to the saturator) is attenuated and output gain is boosted. If @io is < 0, input gain (to the saturator) is boosted and output gain is attenuated. (Boost / attenuation is approximately ± 12dB). This completely reshapes the waveshaping effect.

attributes.name: lowcutoff
attributes.description: Two filters act like a crossover, summing some dry signal back into the saturated path and controlling how much input signal reaches the saturator. @lowcutoff controls the low cut filter (highpass), higher Hz values will make the bass saturation less pronounced.

attributes.name: lowdamp
attributes.description: Two filters act like a crossover, summing some dry signal back into the saturated path and controlling how much input signal reaches the saturator. @lowdamp controls the shelving chracteristic of the low cut (highpass) filter. If @lowdamp == 0, the filter is bypassed, if @lowdamp == 1 the filter is a full highpass and the cutting effect very strong. 0..1 @lowdamp is an increasingly damping shelf filter.

attributes.name: smooth
attributes.description: Optionally smooth the 'drive' inlet (inlet 2) by this amount in ms. This should be turned off (set to 0) if audio rate modulating inlet 2.
